clue.text: Tolerating one's position in society

definitions.meaning: ... a thing means putting up with it, so the word is a participle meaning enduring
a person's rank or reputation among others

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with their social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb and noun stand: to bear something, and a place held in public esteem.

clue.text: Tension leading to silver hair

indicators.note: leading to puts the silver letter in front of the word for hair

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for silver
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Worry ends up giving someone grey hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver hair' reads as grey hair but splits into S and TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain or pressure, mental or physical.

clue.text: An entrance in stone

parts.note: an gives the letter A
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A doorway set in a stone wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded semi-precious variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Defeated in protest march and is held for rioting

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a protest march

indicators.note: rioting suggests the letters of is held running wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Beaten at a demonstration, someone is detained for riotous behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' looks like a container signal but is fodder: 'rioting' rearranges IS HELD into LISHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly beaten, flattened as a building is torn down.

clue.text: The sticky stuff that could, oddly, grow on …

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of grow on

explanation.surface: Something gooey that might, strangely, spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is a thick, viscous substance.

clue.text: Left back in charge, given latitude

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for left from its end to its start

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A left-back footballer put in charge is given freedom on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PORT into TROP. 'Left back' looks like a football position and 'latitude' like freedom, but latitude here is the geographical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Each tropic is a named parallel, a line of latitude about 23 degrees north or south of the equator.

clue.text: …grass right by rising river

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the river name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: Grass growing beside a river that rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses DEE into EED, as a down clue reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall water-side grass-like plant.

clue.text: Type of book on marijuana heating unit?

parts.note: pot is slang for marijuana
a boiler heats water for a house

explanation.surface: A book about cannabis placed on the central heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap, quickly written work produced mainly to earn money.

clue.text: Relaxed about a heartless football official

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the official is removed

parts.note: the referee officiates a football match

explanation.surface: Laid-back about a callous match official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central E of REFEREE, leaving REFREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of worry or responsibility.

clue.text: The province of a genuine Frenchman

parts.note: genuine means real
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French man's title

explanation.surface: A domain that belongs to an authentic Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A province in the sense of a field or domain of activity is a kingdom or sphere.

clue.text: Material from which technical college had to steer away

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a British college of technical higher education

indicators.note: away here means the word steer is knocked out of its order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A technical college has had to steer clear of a certain fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges STEER into ESTER. A POLY (polytechnic) was a British technical college, most renamed universities in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fabric or fibre made from a plastic resin.

clue.text: Doctor to a sporting champion

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of to a sporting are altered

explanation.surface: A physician attending a sports star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here, rearranging TO A SPORTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading advocate or champion of a cause.

clue.text: A railway sketch?

parts.note: read literally, a picture of a train route; really a drawing done only in pen strokes

explanation.definitionFit: A picture made with lines alone, without shading or colour.

clue.text: Hypnotised for a while before spring?

indicators.note: before puts the word for a while ahead of the word for spring

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone is in a trance for a time ahead of the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season but is a leap, BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held under a magic charm is entranced, as if mesmerised.

clue.text: The idiot on the lake should use it!

definitions.text: The idiot on the lake should use it!

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, places the idiot after the lake letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
an oaf is a stupid lout

explanation.surface: A fool out on the water is told to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British rhyming slang (loaf of bread = head) for 'think', which is what the idiot should do.
explanation.definitionFit: In cockney rhyming slang a loaf stands for the head, the thing a fool ought to use.

clue.text: Notice released supporting 9's team

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting places the notice and released below the 9 answer

parts.note: the answer to 9 across gives its letters here
an ad is a notice, an advertisement
rid means freed of, released

explanation.surface: A notice of a release backing a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Real Madrid is a Spanish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is a famous football club from Spain's capital.

clue.text: Newspaper exposé on salts linked to disorder

indicators.note: to disorder something is to jumble it, so the letters of salts and linked are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid revelation about salts tied to some illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges SALTS LINKED; it reads as a medical disorder in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid story in which someone reveals intimate details of an affair with a celebrity.

clue.text: Chef's position to royal army commander in the past

parts.note: a chef works in a kitchen
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A royal cook's station given to an old general.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal of the First World War, famous from recruiting posters.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Kitchener was the British field marshal and war secretary at the start of World War One.

clue.text: A runner from hell's kitchen?

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken from within the words hell's kitchen

explanation.surface: Something that has run out of a notorious kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A runner here is one of a pair of skis, which runs over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner fixed to a boot for gliding on snow.

clue.text: Mix up over 9 with cbs

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Mix up over 9 with cbs (8)': 'cbs' is garbled and no wordplay for SCRAMBLE can be read from it; no source gives the printed text.

clue.text: The day before is always short

indicators.note: short means the word for always loses its final letter

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: The previous day is forever too brief.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening or day preceding an event, as in Christmas Eve.

clue.text: One won't drink and drive here — or tell at offending!

parts.note: in golf the tee is where you drive from

indicators.note: offending suggests the letters of or tell at are put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A warning against drink-driving, or a scolding for misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' reads as driving a car but is a golf drive, taken from the TEE. 'offending' rearranges OR TELL AT into OTALLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcohol.

clue.text: Class that's not so much working

parts.note: less means not so much
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A school period that involves less effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of teaching in a school timetable.

clue.text: Heroin in crack causes pain

indicators.note: in places the letter for heroin inside the word for crack

parts.note: a crack player is an ace, an expert
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Drugs hidden in crack cocaine cause suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug but means expert, ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous hurt in part of the body.

clue.text: Limits are set covering one having to build up a fighting force

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged letters go around the letter for one
set means the letters of limits are are arranged anew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Boundaries are laid down for anyone forced to raise an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges LIMITS ARE into MILTARISE, and 'covering' wraps that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip a country or region with troops and weapons, ready for war.

clue.text: Fool changing the ending, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: changing the ending means the last letter of the word for fool is swapped for another

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool alters how a sentence finishes, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The final T of IDIOT becomes M.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression whose meaning is not literal, a turn of phrase.

clue.text: Lizard point — dangerously wet!

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

indicators.note: dangerously means the letters of wet are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A reptile at a perilously wet spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dangerously' rearranges WET into EWT. The setter loosely calls this amphibian a lizard; it looks like one.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lizard-like amphibian with a long tail.

clue.text: Dust began to settle in a legislative assembly

indicators.note: settle here means the letters of dust began fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Dust began to settle in a parliament chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' rearranges DUST BEGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bundestag is the federal parliament of Germany.

clue.text: A quiet sort of tree?

parts.note: a gives the letter A
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A silent kind of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A common deciduous tree with winged seeds.

clue.text: Helps to chase runs, and attacks

indicators.note: to chase is to come behind, so the word for helps goes after the runs letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
aids means helps

explanation.surface: Assistants go after runs scored in cricket and also assault.
explanation.walkthrough: A run in cricket is a point scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden assaults or incursions on a place.

clue.text: A sailor about to return to make corrections

indicators.note: to return means the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A seaman is about to come back to make amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the whole string ATARRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of mistakes found in a printed book with their fixes.

clue.text: A convenient chap to have around?

definitions.text: A convenient chap to have around?

parts.words: A convenient chap to have around?
parts.note: read literally, a man who is useful or close at hand; the real sense is someone good at odd jobs

explanation.definitionFit: A person skilled at doing small repairs and jobs about the house.
